requirements.requirement: Establish an integrity baseline for /etc on node1 covering its files with reproducible integrity data (checksums/metadata)
requirements.summary: A custom BusyBox-compatible script (/usr/local/sbin/etc-integrity.sh) was created and run in 'generate' mode, producing SHA-256 checksums for 277 files and metadata (perms/owner/size/mtime) for 377 entries under /etc, stored in /var/lib/file-integrity/. Alpine's repos were confirmed to lack AIDE/tripwire/samhain/osquery, justifying the custom approach.

requirements.requirement: The baseline must be usable to identify/report later changes to /etc files
requirements.summary: A 'verify' subcommand was implemented and validated: after appending to /etc/motd and adding /etc/newly-added-test-file, verify correctly flagged the modified file ('./motd: FAILED') and listed the new file separately, directly demonstrating change-detection capability.

requirements.requirement: A clean, accurate baseline should be left in place on node1 (not contaminated by test artifacts)
requirements.summary: Test changes (motd append, new test file) were reverted and the baseline was regenerated; a subsequent verify run showed zero checksum diffs and zero new files, confirming a clean final baseline state.

requirements.requirement: Baseline and node remain intact/usable after the provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (15f3a3af...) and healthy baseline state were captured, reboot was acknowledged (backgrounded sleep+reboot returned immediately), connection was lost then reconnected with a distinct post-restart boot_id (c10061fb...) and reset uptime (31.88s), and the baseline files were confirmed present with identical SHA-256 hashes and a clean verify run afterward. This is corroborated by the fixed global boot-identity observations (before_prepare vs after_executor), which independently show the same boot_id transition.

overall_summary: The executor established a functional, tested integrity baseline for /etc on node1 using a custom SHA-256/metadata script since no AIDE-like package was available, validated its change-detection capability via a falsification test, restored a clean baseline afterward, and completed the mandatory restart evidence protocol showing a genuine boot-identity change with intact baseline data post-restart. All material task outcomes are directly and coherently supported by evidence.
limitations: No direct evidence of automated/scheduled periodic verification (e.g., cron) was captured; the task only required establishing the baseline, and this was not claimed as a requirement, but ongoing automatic reporting is not demonstrated.
A minor leftover file (/tmp/reboot.log) from the restart mechanism was not cleaned up, though it is inconsequential.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were nearly all discovery, tool creation, or bounded/reverted test mutations directly tied to the task. 'apk update' and failed 'apk add aide/tripwire/etc' attempts (cmd-fa77fe267a5e48ea, cmd-4ccb41edf2094e56, cmd-d9f6e53080fd414f) were reasonable discovery to justify the custom-script approach and did not damage package state (no packages were installed, only the index cache refreshed). The falsification test (motd append + new file, cmd-9da497a989e24e15) was a bounded, low-risk mutation fully reverted with a regenerated clean baseline (cmd-9397b7f821aa4329). The restart itself (cmd-6f34e2185a31435c) was required by the separate node-restart evidence protocol and left node1 in a healthy, verified state. One minor residue remains: /tmp/reboot.log (from the backgrounded reboot command) was left behind, visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot, a trivial and expected artifact of the restart mechanism rather than an unnecessary mutation.
